classification.difficultyReason: Requires sketching a familiar parabola and directly applying the supplied reflection and vertical-translation forms, keeping the three vertices and opening directions consistent on shared axes.

content.prompt:
Let $f(x)=x^2-2$.

Sketch the graphs of $y=f(x)$, $y=-f(x)$ and $y=f(x)+3$ on the one set of axes.

answer.short:
$y=f(x)=x^2-2$, $y=-f(x)=2-x^2$ and $y=f(x)+3=x^2+1$.

Their vertices are $(0,-2)$, $(0,2)$ and $(0,1)$ respectively; see the shared graph.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}-f(x)&=-(x^2-2)\\-f(x)&=2-x^2\\f(x)+3&=x^2-2+3\\f(x)+3&=x^2+1\end{align*}$$
Sketch $y=f(x)$ with vertex $(0,-2)$ and intercepts $(\pm\sqrt2,0)$. Reflect this curve in the $x$-axis to obtain $y=-f(x)$, with vertex $(0,2)$ and the same $x$-intercepts. Translate the original curve upwards 3 units to obtain $y=f(x)+3$, with vertex $(0,1)$ and no $x$-intercepts. Draw and label all three curves on the same axes.

spec.description: Three equation-driven parabolas on shared axes. Solid, dashed and dotted strokes distinguish the labelled curves. No grid or axes are supplied in the student question.
spec.mathematics: y=x^2-2 has vertex (0,-2); y=2-x^2 has vertex (0,2); y=x^2+1 has vertex (0,1). The first two cross the x-axis at plus or minus sqrt(2).
spec.answerVisibility: All curves and labels are solution-only.
